examples.title: Solving a quadratic
steps: Split the middle term using two numbers with product 6 × (−2) = −12 and sum −1: these are −4 and 3.
Set each factor to zero: x = −1/2 or x = 2/3.

examples.title: Sum and product of roots
examples.problem: One root of x² − 11x + k = 0 is 4. Find k and the other root.
steps: The roots add up to 11, so the other root is 11 − 4 = 7.
The product of the roots is k, so k = 4 × 7 = 28.
examples.answer: k = 28, and the other root is 7

examples.title: Expressions in α and β
examples.problem: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 6x + 1 = 0, find 1/α² + 1/β².

examples.title: Using the discriminant
examples.problem: For which values of k does kx² + 6x + 3 = 0 have two different real roots?
steps: The equation must stay quadratic, so k cannot be 0.
Two different real roots need 36 − 12k > 0, so k < 3.
Putting both together: k < 3 and k ≠ 0.

examples.title: Maximum and minimum value
steps: The x² term is negative, so the expression has a greatest value, at x = −b/2a = −12/(−4) = 3.
